macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks near record highs as investors await Fed signals
items.summary: U.S. stock-index futures were little changed on Sunday after a relatively quiet week, with investors watching for clues from the Federal Reserve on the path of interest rates. Earlier in the week, major U.S. indexes had been hovering near record levels as softer inflation data supported expectations that the Fed would hold rates steady in September.

items.title: China July industrial output slows; retail sales rise modestly
items.summary: China's industrial output grew 4.5% year over year in July, down from 5.3% in June, while retail sales increased 0.6%, highlighting mixed momentum in the world's second-largest economy. Broader data also showed M2 money supply growth of 7.7%, below expectations, suggesting somewhat softer monetary expansion.
items.source: Reuters via Yahoo Finance / JPMHK Warrants newsfeed

items.title: U.S. inflation remained subdued in July, reinforcing rate-cut expectations
items.summary: U.S. inflation cooled to 3.4% in July, and traders interpreted the latest price data as supporting a Federal Reserve pause at its September meeting. Treasury yields and equity futures moved on the view that softer inflation reduces the odds of an imminent rate hike.
items.source: The Wall Street Journal / Economic Times

items.title: S&P 500 and Nasdaq gained on strong tech earnings and softer inflation
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended higher after upbeat quarterly results from CoreWeave and other AI infrastructure firms, while mild inflation data strengthened the case for the Fed to keep rates unchanged in September. The S&P 500 rose 0.26% to 7,748.58, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.55% to 26,588.49.

items.title: S&P 500 hits record close as tame producer prices lift sentiment
items.summary: The S&P 500 set a record-high close on Thursday, led by gains in Sandisk and other large technology stocks, after tame producer price inflation supported expectations that the Fed would not raise rates at its September meeting. Risk appetite improved broadly across equities.

items.title: Treasury yields and futures react to softer inflation and Fed outlook
items.summary: U.S. Treasury yields held recent gains after the latest inflation report and a strong 10-year note auction, with the 10-year yield near 4.68% to 4.70%. Futures pricing suggested a slight majority expecting the Fed to leave rates unchanged in September.

items.title: Indian rupee weakens after RBI trims FX swap window
items.summary: The Indian rupee fell to 95.59 per dollar in early Monday trade after the Reserve Bank of India shortened its zero-cost FX swap facility for banks. Traders said the move increased caution in the currency market.

items.title: Hong Kong and mainland China shares rose on upbeat regional sentiment
items.summary: Asian markets were broadly firmer, with Hong Kong and Shanghai indexes both posting gains amid signs of stability in regional growth and trade. The move followed weaker Japan growth data and a modestly softer U.S. rate backdrop.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major altcoins were mostly flat to slightly higher in a muted 24-hour session
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around the $63.1K-$63.5K area, with Ethereum near $1.9K, XRP near $1.00, and Solana around $75, while the total crypto market cap stayed roughly in the $2.2T range. Several market recaps described the session as sideways consolidation, with Bitcoin up modestly on the day but still down on the week.
items.source: CryptoRank / TradingView / Forbes Digital Assets / CoinStats

items.title: SEC and U.S. regulators remained active on crypto market structure and stablecoin rules
items.summary: Reports said the SEC is planning a regulatory path for 24/7 tokenized stocks, while the U.S. Treasury is seeking feedback on new GENIUS Act stablecoin rules. Another report said the SEC canceled a vote on crypto startup rules, underscoring continued policy uncertainty.

items.title: Tether completed its first full financial audit after years of scrutiny
items.summary: Tether announced completion of its first full financial audit, a notable development for the USDT issuer after years of pressure over reserve transparency. The news came alongside broader market attention to stablecoin regulation and issuer disclosures.

items.title: Israel’s Bits of Gold reportedly suffered a breach affecting 200,000 customers
items.summary: A major security incident involving Israel’s largest crypto broker, Bits of Gold, reportedly exposed data tied to about 200,000 customers. The breach was highlighted as one of the most significant crypto-related security stories in the last day.

items.title: Ripple minted 10 million RLUSD as supply continued to expand
items.summary: Ripple’s stablecoin RLUSD saw another issuance round, with reports saying 10 million tokens were minted and total supply reached about 1.71 billion. The development adds to ongoing project-level activity around Ripple’s stablecoin rollout.

items.title: Harmony said it plans a chain rollback after forged ONE spread across the network
items.summary: Project news centered on Harmony, which reportedly said it plans a chain rollback after forged ONE tokens spread across the network. The incident points to continued operational and security challenges for smaller blockchain ecosystems.

items.title: Binance reportedly gave Russia-related data used in a Ukraine donation case
items.summary: Reuters-reported allegations said Binance shared client data with Moscow that was later used in a case involving Ukraine-related crypto donations. The report adds to ongoing regulatory and geopolitical pressure on major exchanges.

items.title: Binance will stop transactions involving HTX, EXMO and nine other platforms
items.summary: Binance announced it will stop transactions involving HTX, EXMO, and nine other crypto platforms starting August 23. The move is another sign of tightening exchange compliance and counterparty controls.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly eyes up to $3B investment in SB Energy for OpenAI Ohio data center
items.summary: Reuters reports that Nvidia is in talks to invest as much as $3 billion in SB Energy, a SoftBank subsidiary tied to a large planned Ohio data center project for OpenAI. The report underscores how AI infrastructure spending remains a major industry theme, with chipmakers, cloud builders, and financiers all deepening their commitments.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 3.7 Flash for coding and agent workflows
items.summary: Reuters also notes Google’s release of Gemini 3.7 Flash, a new model aimed at coding and agentic workflows. The launch signals continued rapid iteration in mid-tier frontier models, especially for developer tools and task automation.

items.title: DeepSeek launches V4 Pro and raises pricing for API access
items.summary: Reuters and other outlets report that DeepSeek introduced V4 Pro and increased pricing, with some plans costing up to 14 times more than the prior Flash tier. The move suggests growing monetization pressure even among fast-moving Chinese model providers.

items.title: Stripe reportedly finalizes acquisition of OpenRouter for more than $7 billion
items.summary: TechCrunch and other outlets report that Stripe has finalized a deal to acquire OpenRouter, an AI model gateway startup, for over $7 billion. If completed as reported, the deal would be a major sign that the routing and aggregation layer for model access is becoming strategically important.

items.title: Groq raises $350 million as it pivots from AI chips toward a neocloud business
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Groq raised $350 million at a $3.5 billion valuation while expanding its Nvidia-powered data center footprint. The company’s shift highlights a broader trend in AI infrastructure: startups are moving from pure hardware plays toward cloud capacity and inference services.

items.title: Microsoft delays Exchange CU1 again as AI tools surface security issues
items.summary: Computerworld reports that Microsoft postponed a key Exchange Server update after AI tools uncovered flaws faster than teams could validate them. The delay reflects how AI-assisted security review is increasing both detection speed and verification workload in enterprise software.

items.title: Nvidia financing push for AI infrastructure expands across major banks
items.summary: Multiple outlets report that Nvidia is working with major financial institutions to mobilize large-scale capital for AI infrastructure projects. The development reinforces the industry-wide shift from model announcements to the financing of power, chips, and data centers at global scale.

items.title: Industry chatter points to stronger demand for open-weight and infrastructure-heavy AI
items.summary: Recent coverage highlights debate around open-weight models, major capital commitments to data centers, and platform-level AI acquisitions. Together, these stories point to an industry trend where control of distribution, compute, and model access is becoming as important as model quality itself.
